subject: Export & productization: output title and training carveouts for NovaNet POC
messages:
From: Jill Turner <jill.turner@novanet.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@novanet.com
Date: 2026-11-20T08:15:00Z
Subject: Clarifying output title & export constraints for NovaNet POC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a couple of legal questions before we finalize the POC order form. Two things to clarify on IP/usage:

1) Output title / productization — NovaNet intends to surface generated content (summaries and recommended actions) inside our product that will be customer-facing. We need to understand whether we would own the outputs or if Redwood claims any title when outputs are used in a product.

2) Training / feedback license — we prefer that customer conversational logs are not used to train models without explicit consent. We can accept an aggregated telemetry/quality-improvement clause but want it limited and auditable.

Also, because some outputs may include regulated customer data, we need to confirm any export control responsibilities (we are EU-based and have EU customers). See attached export control questionnaire.

Can you share proposed Order Form language that covers these points (output title, training opt-in, export control liabilities)? We need this back to move to internal legal review.

Best,
Jill

Attachments: NovaNet_export_control_qs.pdf (2 pages)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@novanet.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying output title & export constraints for NovaNet POC

Hi Jill,

Appreciate the clear list — helpful. Looping in Ben (Sales Ops) and Laura (Legal) to propose concrete language. High level options we typically offer:

- Output title: Customer retains title to outputs and may use them in products and for downstream commercialization. Redwood disclaims ownership of customer-provided inputs and customer-generated outputs.

- Training / feedback: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and prompt/response metadata for model quality improvements. Redwood will not train models on customer content (raw inputs or outputs) unless the customer explicitly opts in via a separate addendum or SOW.

- Export control: We normally include a mutual compliance clause and require customers to confirm they will not direct Redwood to undertake export-restricted processing. For EU customers we can add an export-controls appendix that clarifies responsibilities and adds an indemnity limited to willful breaches.

I attached an initial redline with these points called priyom_proposed_redlines.docx — Laura, could you suggest precise legal wording for the order form / MSA carveouts? Jill, happy to set a 30-min call today to walk legal through the options. Are you available at 4pm CET?

Next steps: Laura to propose wording; I'll sync with Ben on contract cadence for the POC.

Thanks,
Priyom

Attachments: priyom_proposed_redlines.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jill Turner <jill.turner@novanet.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifying output title & export constraints for NovaNet POC

Priyom / Ben / Jill —

Thanks for the context. Below are suggested clauses we can drop into the Order Form (Option A = customer-forward rights; Option B = narrower productization carveout). I'm keeping language short so Procurement can review quickly.

PROPOSED CLAUSES (draft language)

1) Output Ownership
"Customer Content" means Customer-provided inputs and Customer-Generated Outputs.
"Customer-Generated Outputs": outputs (including but not limited to text, summaries, embeddings, or classification results) produced by the Services in response to Customer Content.

"Ownership": Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and Customer-Generated Outputs. Redwood shall have no ownership or title in Customer Content or Customer-Generated Outputs, and Customer may use, reproduce, publish, distribute and otherwise commercialize Customer-Generated Outputs.

2) Feedback and Training License
Redwood may collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and usage metrics to improve the Services. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer-Generated Outputs to train models or for other model-weight updates unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in (e.g., an executed Training Addendum). Any such opt-in will be subject to mutually agreed terms.

3) Export Controls and Compliance
Each party shall comply with applicable export control laws. Customer represents and warrants that it will not provide Redwood with any data or instructions that would require Redwood to violate applicable export control laws. To the extent outputs are later subject to export controls due to Customer use, Customer will be responsible for compliance and indemnify Redwood for claims resulting from Customer's willful violation. Redwood will cooperate with commercially reasonable requests to support Customer compliance (e.g., providing telemetry summaries).

Redlines / practical notes:
- We should avoid absolute blanket training bans; offering an "explicit opt-in" path is standard and protects both sides.
- For EU customers, consider an export-control appendix that references EU sanctions lists and includes mutual representations.
- If NovaNet needs the right to productize outputs but wants stronger auditability, we can add a telemetry audit right for a narrow retention window.

If this looks OK I can convert to tracked changes in the attached redline and propose the MSA/Order Form cross-reference. Priyom — please confirm whether we want Option A (full output title) or Option B (limited productization license) for this deal.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
